description: Construction number 113547319. Photographed on display by Richard Vandervord 6 September 2024; Wrecks and Relics Online still lists it present August 2026.
Wears the single-digit Egyptian serial 1. Photographed at Almaza by Graham Hutchinson in 2020 and by Richard Vandervord in September 2024.

Egyptian licence development of the Bucker Bu 181 Bestmann. Wrecks and Relics Online notes the airframe carries no serial on the fuselage; the identity 100 comes from that compilation rather than from a visible marking.
Photographed carrying 383 at Almaza by Graham Hutchinson in 2020. Wrecks and Relics Online last noted August 2026. aviationmuseum.eu gives 382 which the photograph contradicts.

Construction number 3048. Displayed wearing the false serial 67289; Wrecks and Relics Online records the marking explicitly as "As 67289" and gives 7827 as the true Egyptian serial. One of the Peace Pharaoh F-4Es transferred from the USAF in 1979.

Construction number BD-35. Photographed on display by Richard Vandervord 6 September 2024. Manufacturer attribution follows airhistory.net; gmap.nl credits General Dynamics and the correct attribution depends on a delivery date that was not established.
Construction number 5189. Listed by Wrecks and Relics Online as present August 2026.

Egypt assembled and later built the HA-200 at Helwan as the Al Kahira. Whether this airframe is Spanish-built or Helwan-built was not established so the manufacturer is given as the design originator.

Construction number V-3. The Messerschmitt-designed Egyptian supersonic fighter prototype. Photographed by Richard Vandervord 6 September 2024 and by Graham Hutchinson in 2020. The other two HA-300 airframes are in Germany at Oberschleissheim and Manching so this is the only one left in Egypt.

True identity not established. Wrecks and Relics Online records the airframe as displayed "As 1101" which is a marking rather than a confirmed serial so tail_number is left blank. aviationmuseum.eu reports the same number as if it were the serial.

Egyptian K-8E assembled by the Arab Organization for Industrialization. Wrecks and Relics Online gives the serial only as ".../1" so none is recorded. Photographed by Richard Vandervord 6 September 2024.

Photographed by Graham Hutchinson in 2020 and Richard Vandervord in September 2024. aviationmuseum.eu conflates this airframe with the museum Su-20 and gives its serial as 7770.

Photographed by Richard Vandervord 6 September 2024. The Cairo Citadel Su-7BMK is displayed wearing this same number 7751 as a false marking which is the origin of a long-standing confusion between the two Cairo museums.

Photographed as 7770 at Almaza by Graham Hutchinson in 2020 and by Richard Vandervord in September 2024 as an airframe distinct from Su-7BMK 7001 and Su-17K 7751. Wrecks and Relics Online omits this aircraft from its Almaza list entirely; the photographs are the correction.

Construction number 63400704. The largest airframe in the collection. Photographed by Graham Hutchinson in 2020 and Richard Vandervord in September 2024. Sources disagree on the sub-variant with airhistory.net giving Tu-16KS and aviationmuseum.eu giving Tu-16D/G so the variant field is left blank.
